content.rendered:
Talk about elusive: we know of at least four documented occasions on which Bruce covered Chuck Berry’s seminal “Roll Over Beethoven” from as early as 1971 through 2002, but no one managed to capture it on tape until a fan requested it during the Working on a Dream Tour in 2009.

Here’s that performance from St. Louis:

It’s a bit surprising that Bruce didn’t give us more opportunities to catch “Roll Over Beethoven” in concert. We know he’s a big fan of Chuck Berry after all, and besides: how could a young rock musician resist an anthem that loudly proclaimed the arrival and power of rock and roll? (He couldn’t–two of his first four performances of the song took place long before Bruce garnered national attention.)

Berry’s 1956 original wasn’t a huge hit upon initial release–it didn’t even crack the Top 40 in the U.S. But “Roll Over Beethoven” was hugely influential, and Rolling Stone now ranks it at a very high #97 in its 500 Greatest Songs of All Time.

Nevertheless, besides a 2017 Asbury Park jam session mash-up appearance, that 2009 performance is our only opportunity to hear Bruce perform it.

Roll Over Beethoven
First performed: May 14, 1971 (Asbury Park, NJ)
Last performed: April 21, 2017 (Asbury Park, NJ)

© August 8, 2019

excerpt.rendered: Bruce covered it several times over the years, as far back as 1971–but it took until 2009 before a taper could capture Bruce covering Chuck Berry’s seminal classic, “Roll Over Beethoven.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rock and Roll Music
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce leads an all-star line-up on a raucous cover of Chuck Berry's "Rock and Roll Music."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Johnny B. Goode
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: From the 1995 opening concert for the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame: Chuck Berry backed by Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Around and Around
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Many, many times--but almost always in small clubs: Bruce rocks the house with a cover of Chuck Berry's classic B-side, "Around and Around."

jetpack-related-posts.title: September 2
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The Human Rights Now! Tour kicks off, Bruce and Bob Seger meet for the first time, Bruce and the E Street Band help inaugurate the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and more.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Shake, Rattle and Roll
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: A rusty E Street Band lumbered through their first attempt at Big Joe Turner's rock and roll standard, but they more than made up for it 18 years later.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Sweet Little Sixteen
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Watch a great pro-shot video of Bruce covering Chuck Berry's classic 20 years after its release.
